question: Should OpenClaw add a generic action-aware tool-policy contract for multiplexed tools, and what trusted bypass semantics should approved workflows use?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the fix defines a new authorization boundary and config grammar that can change operator security posture across message, gateway, sender, sandbox, plugin, and HTTP invocation paths.

options.title: Design generic action policy
options.body: Add a typed action-aware policy grammar enforced before multiplexed tool actions execute, with documented precedence and trusted-context tests for message and gateway.

options.title: Narrow to message and gateway
options.body: Add separate action controls only for the currently affected tools, reducing immediate scope but creating parallel policy surfaces that may drift.

options.title: Defer to confirmation work
options.body: Rely on the adjacent confirmation-gate design and accept that static least-privilege action deny remains unavailable for now.

recommendation.title: Design generic action policy
recommendation.body: Add a typed action-aware policy grammar enforced before multiplexed tool actions execute, with documented precedence and trusted-context tests for message and gateway.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete is the live review participant and recent adjacent contributor for the policy, message, and gateway surfaces involved in the decision.
